guide_enrichment.narrative:
We see Texas’ passing game as the clearest source of separation. Arch Manning opened the season by completing 20 of 27 passes for 305 yards and four touchdowns, while Texas generated 516 total yards at 7.0 yards per play. We are not treating one result as proof of another blowout, but it supports the broader matchup signal in our numbers.

The counterweight is that this is not a completely one-sided efficiency profile. Our data gives UT San Antonio’s passing offense a plausible path to move the ball against the Texas pass defense, and we do not see the same clear advantage for Texas in creating scoring opportunities. Texas has forced a turnover in 24 consecutive home games, but turnovers can widen a margin without being something we want to price as automatic.

For us, the case for Texas is easy to understand: superior passing efficiency can create separation quickly. The problem is that the market already accounts for that advantage, while the less decisive areas leave little room for error. We do not see enough value beyond the football case, so we are passing.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Manning and the Texas receivers against the UT San Antonio pass defense. Ryan Wingo produced seven catches for 121 yards and a touchdown in the opener, while Cam Coleman added 70 yards and two scores in his Texas debut. With four 2025 offensive-line starters back, Texas has the supporting structure to press its most favorable matchup; the question for us is whether that advantage produces enough sustained separation to exceed an already demanding market expectation.

recent_game.fact: Texas opened the 2026 season with a 59-7 home win over Texas State on Sept. 5.
Texas produced 516 total yards and averaged 7.0 yards per play against Texas State.
Texas forced three turnovers against Texas State, recovering two fumbles and making one interception.

opponent_notes.fact: Against UTSA in 2024, Arch Manning entered after Quinn Ewers was injured and recorded a 67-yard touchdown run and a 75-yard touchdown pass to Ryan Wingo.
Manning accounted for five touchdowns against UTSA in 2024, including four passing touchdowns and one rushing touchdown.

quarterback.fact: Senior quarterback Arch Manning completed 20 of 27 passes for 305 yards and four touchdowns in the 2026 opener against Texas State.
Manning is 13-3 as a starter and 9-0 as a starter at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium.
In 13 starts during 2025, Manning completed 248 of 404 passes for 3,163 yards and 26 touchdowns and added 399 rushing yards and a team-high 10 rushing touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Running backs Raleek Brown and Hollywood Smothers transferred to Texas in spring 2026 from Arizona State and NC State, respectively.
Smothers recorded 72 rushing yards and added three receptions for 28 yards and a touchdown against Texas State, totaling 100 yards from scrimmage.
Brown had 11 carries for 34 yards and two touchdowns in his Texas debut against Texas State.
Ryan Wingo caught seven passes for 121 yards and one touchdown against Texas State.
Auburn transfer Cam Coleman made his Texas debut with three receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns against Texas State.
Texas returns 2025 offensive-line starters Trevor Goosby, Brandon Baker, Cole Hutson and Connor Robertson.
Texas added offensive linemen Laurence Seymore III, Melvin Siani and Dylan Sikorski through the transfer portal for 2026.
The nine offensive linemen listed in the guide entered 2026 with a combined 226 games played and 114 starts.
Texas added fifth-year tight end Michael Masunas from Michigan State; he played in all 12 games with eight starts and recorded 19 catches for 232 yards and three touchdowns in 2025.

defensive_personnel.fact: Edge Colin Simmons recorded one tackle, a half tackle for loss, one quarterback hurry and a fumble recovery against Texas State.
Simmons led Texas in 2025 with 15.5 tackles for loss, 12 sacks, 15 pressures and three forced fumbles; his 12 sacks led the SEC.
Texas added defensive transfers Rasheem Biles, Markus Boswell, Justin Cryer, Darius Snow, Ian Geffrard, Zion Williams, Bo Mascoe and Nick Hudson for the 2026 season.

coaching_changes.fact: Will Muschamp is Texas' defensive coordinator, with Johnny Nansen serving as co-defensive coordinator and linebackers coach.
Kyle Flood is Texas' offensive coordinator and offensive line coach, while AJ Milwee is co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.

offensive_context.fact: Texas rushed for 156 yards and three touchdowns against Texas State.
Texas did not punt against Texas State, its first game without a punt since the 2023 game against Kansas.
Texas is 26-2 when scoring first since the beginning of the 2023 season.

defensive_context.fact: Texas has forced a turnover in 24 consecutive home games, identified in the guide as the longest active streak in the FBS.
Texas has forced a turnover in 36 of its last 37 games.
Texas recorded 21 takeaways in 2025, including 16 interceptions.
Texas recorded at least 40 sacks and 15 interceptions in both 2024 and 2025.

series_context.fact: The 2026 game will be the third meeting between Texas and UTSA, with all three meetings played in Austin.
Texas defeated UTSA 41-20 in 2022 and 56-7 in 2024.

other_relevant.fact: Thirty-three players made their Texas debut in the 59-7 season-opening win over Texas State.
Texas added 22 transfers from other colleges for the 2026 season.
